comment: Paper claims halogenation of both L- and D-tryptophan but no evidence provided. Associated MIBiG entry BGC0000382 shows no gene for putative halogenase and no pathway-specific flavin reductase identified.

changelog.comment: New entry. Removed wrong cofactor. Corrected some spelling mistakes.

reactions.description: Lysine activates HOCl, which attacks L-tryptophan to form a Wheland intermediate. Aromaticity is restored through deprotonation by a glutamate residue, yielding 6-chloro-tryptophan or 6-bromo-tryptophan.
Chlorination of anthranilic acid to C5-chloro-anthranilic acid
Chlorination of N-phenylanthranilic acid to N-phenylanthranilic acid
